svg.aria-label: Diagram: AWS Certificate Manager grants automatic renewal on the basis of use rather than issuance. Every eligible case in the published list describes a certificate that was associated with another AWS service or exported since being issued or last renewed, including the two private-certificate cases where AWS states that issuing is not enough. Three cases are not eligible: a private certificate issued by calling the AWS Private CA IssueCertificate API, an imported certificate, and one that has already expired. Both DNS and email validation support renewal: DNS renews unattended while the validation records remain in place, while email validation sends the domain owner a link to click 45 days before expiry, since renewing a certificate requires action by the domain owner. Certificates issued through ACME are not eligible for ACM managed renewal because renewal is managed by the ACME client, and ACME certificates cannot be used with AWS integrated services.
svg.title: Renewal is earned by use, not granted by issuance
svg.text: Issuance does not appear anywhere in the eligibility test.
AWS Certificate Manager — managed renewal, read as a list rather than as a promise.
ELIGIBLE — four entries, two verbs
“associated with another AWS service, such as
Elastic Load Balancing or CloudFront”
“exported since being issued or last renewed”
Private via ACM RequestCertificate “and then
exported or associated” · same via the console
AWS spells out that issuing it is not enough.
NOT ELIGIBLE — three, and one has no recovery
“a private certificate issued by calling the AWS
Private CA IssueCertificate API”
“if imported”
“if already expired”
The others can be fixed before they bite. By the time
this one applies, the outage has started.
The row that is not in AWS’s list, and follows from it
ISSUED AND UNUSED meets no eligible condition → does not renew, and looks identical in the console
Nothing says an unused certificate will not renew. The list simply never makes it eligible.
That reading is mine. The four eligible entries are AWS’s.
Both validation methods renew. One is unattended.
DNS renews automatically while the records stay
EMAIL a link to click, 45 days before expiry
“Renewing a certificate requires action by the
domain owner.”
Email costs unattendedness, not renewal.
ACME: a different path, a different owner
“not eligible for ACM managed renewal. Renewal
… is managed by the ACME client”
“cannot be used with AWS integrated services”
CertificateKeyPairOrigin: ACME | AWS_MANAGED | CUSTOMER_PROVIDED
Two facts that make renewal easy to live with — and one that catches multi-Region
“the certificate’s Amazon Resource Name (ARN) remains the same” — so a renewal churns no references.
“ACM certificates are regional resources … each of these certificates must be renewed independently.”
The audit: certificates attached to nothing, never exported — run it per Region.
The failover Region is where staged, unattached certificates collect, and it is the one nobody checks until the day
they need it.
Alarm on expiry outside ACM: the one state it will not fix is the one you most need telling about.
